title: Genomic profiling of anaplastic meningioma identifies recurrent genetic alterations with relevance to lower-grade meningioma

needs_manual_review_reason: PER-SAMPLE DATA UPDATE (2026-07-10): Per-sample diagnosis/tumor-type/radiation data recovered from family.soft. All 8 samples are anaplastic (WHO grade III) meningioma -- single-grade cohort, so no grade_breakdown comparison is possible, but this is now confirmed rather than inferred from the title alone. RADIATION DATA: radiation field per-sample: 3 no, 5 yes -- extracted from family.soft. RECURRENCE DATA: tumor type field per-sample: 3 Primary, 5 Secondary (i.e. recurrent) -- extracted from family.soft, out of 8 total anaplastic meningioma samples. Series-level GEO metadata verified directly against the live source; per-sample clinical/pathology fields (grade, sex/age, anatomic location, brain invasion, treatment timepoint) have not yet been extracted from individual GSM records or supplementary tables -- part of the batch-1 scaling pass, prioritizing breadth of verified accessions over per-sample depth. Publication metadata pulled from PubMed esummary; not yet manually spot-checked against the full text for every record in this batch. FACT-CHECK UPDATE (2026-07-10 verification pass): tissue_preservation filled in as 'fresh_frozen', previously 'Not reported'. Series_overall_design states 'Eight cases of anaplastic meningioma with snap frozen tissue underwent RNA sequencing.' COMPLETENESS FIX (2026-07-11 fact-check pass): treatment_timepoint_status was left at 'Not reported' even though this record's own note above already documents an explicit per-sample primary-vs-recurrent breakdown (3 Primary, 5 Secondary/recurrent, from the family.soft 'tumor type' field), consistent with tags.recurrence_annotated already being true; corrected to ['primary', 'recurrent'] to match. COMPLETENESS FIX (2026-07-13, prompted by an audit of the radiation_timepoint tag corpus-wide): tags.radiation_timepoint was already correctly true, but treatment_timepoint_status had never been updated to reflect the radiation dimension this record's own 'RADIATION DATA' note above already documented. Re-verified directly against the live GEO family.soft per-sample data: every one of the 3 'Primary'/radiation:no samples and every one of the 5 'Secondary'(recurrent)/radiation:yes samples correlate perfectly (radiation:yes occurs only alongside tumor type:Secondary), confirming this is genuine post-radiotherapy-treatment recurrence data (radiotherapy given after the primary tumor, before the recurrence sample was later collected) -- true treatment timing, not a radiation-induced-etiology cohort-selection criterion (see the correction made the same day on the unrelated Agnihotri RIM records, where that distinction was found to matter). Added pre_radiation/post_radiation to treatment_timepoint_status to match. CONFIDENCE CAVEAT (2026-07-13, prompted by direct user follow-up questioning how this was known): re-checked the raw evidence honestly rather than resting on the prior pass. The GEO per-sample field is literally just 'radiation: yes/no' correlated 1:1 with 'tumor type: Primary/Secondary' -- that correlation alone is ambiguous between treatment timing and radiation-induced etiology (the same shape of ambiguity that caused the Agnihotri RIM misclassification). The paper is a letter with no PubMed abstract and no open-access full text, so no sentence stating what 'radiation' refers to could be found. The read given here (post-radiotherapy recurrence, i.e. treatment timing) rests on the Series_summary's stated premise -- 'paired primary and recurrent meningiomas... evolution of anaplastic meningioma from lower-grade precursor tumours' -- which is about primary-to-recurrent genomic evolution, with no radiation-induced-etiology language anywhere in the title/summary/design (unlike the RIM papers, which state that premise outright). This is a lower-confidence inference from context, not a directly confirming sentence; flagged here explicitly so this record isn't mistaken for the same evidentiary strength as figshare-32043249-methylation-project's priorRT/adjuvantRT columns (which are confirmed via the linked GitHub survival-analysis code treating radiotherapy as a time-dependent covariate). AUDIT PASS (2026-07-14): per instructions from the prior 2026-07-13 caveat, treatment_timepoint_status/tags.radiation_timepoint were left untouched -- no new full-text access was obtained (Wiley page for doi.org/10.1111/nan.12487 returned HTTP 403; PubMed/Europe PMC still show no abstract for this letter), so nothing changed there. Other fields re-verified live: (1) publications[0] author list re-checked against both PubMed efetch XML and Europe PMC core record -- both independently confirm the exact same 6 authors (Cimino PJ, Yoda RA, Wirsching H-G, Warrick JI, Dorschner MO, Ferreira M) with no additional authors past #6, so this is a genuine 6-author paper, NOT an instance of the corpus's known 6-author-truncation bug; no author-list change made. corresponding_author could not be confirmed or refuted (no correspondence footnote accessible; left unchanged). (3) Re-checked two individual GSM records (GSM5280835, GSM5280840) directly for any molecular-subtype/driver-mutation or outcome/survival fields beyond diagnosis/tumor type/tissue/radiation -- none present, confirming molecular_subtype_annotated and has_outcome_data remain correctly false/Not reported (not an instance of the 'real data hiding in full text' failure pattern, since full text itself is inaccessible, and GEO per-sample fields plainly contain nothing further).
